findings.basis: Each of these 22 profiles falls into one of three groups, and none has a basis that can be checked as a real setting for a real SIM. (a) 11 profiles key a network ID that no commercial SIM reports: a two-digit MNC under MCC 310/311 (310-00, 310-01, 310-02, 310-09, 310-30, 310-70, 310-88, 310-90, 311-00, 311-03), where US SIMs carry three-digit MNCs, or a three-digit MNC in France (208-090). They come from vendor.xml entries written as mnc="30", "70", "90" and so on, which DefaultCarrierConfigService matches by exact string (DefaultCarrierConfigService.java:360-364). On the source devices they therefore never applied to a real SIM, and the display names (for example 'Verizon' on 310-00, 'ATT Broadband' on 310-70/90) are guesses. (b) 7 profiles have an identity that cannot be tied to a carrier: 262-88, 262-99 and 460-19 with no name and no Google entry, and 234-53/234-54 including the SPN 'GTE' variants (Google's carrier list maps 234-53 to tango_us). Their only basis is Sony vendor.xml (2019-2023). (c) 4 profiles take the value only from old Pixel vendor CarrierSettings: Fi US on 234-20 and 312-580 (marlin/sailfish baseline), Spectrum CHA_ESIM 314-020 and Verizon on-site LTE 999-480 (bramble/redfin, 2024). Google's current CarrierSettings for the same SIMs (google_us, h3_gb, spectrummso_us, verizononsitelte_us) leaves the key unset, so the newer data from the same source does not confirm the value.
findings.effect: rtt_supported_bool (CarrierConfigManager.java:3415-3418, default false at :12190) is read in four places that change call handling. (1) ImsManager.updateRttConfigValue (frameworks/opt/net/ims ImsManager.java:2756-2797): with the key true and ignore_rtt_mode_setting_bool at its default true (CarrierConfigManager.java:11996) it provisions RTT_SETTING_ENABLED=1 into the ImsService and keeps IMS turned on even when nothing else needs it (ImsManager.java:1763-1785); with false it provisions 0. (2) The AOSP ImsStack's ImsRegistrationTracker adds Capability.TEXT next to every VOICE capability when that provisioning item is 1, using rtt_supported_while_roaming_bool when roaming (ImsRegistrationTracker.java:419-424, 585-598), so the normal REGISTER carries the text media feature tag; AosRegistration.UpdateNetworkFeatureRtt marks TEXT unavailable when the network does not confirm it (AosRegistration.cpp:1210-1245). (3) The native stack reads the key directly (CarrierConfig.java:62-90 forwards it; AosNConfiguration.cpp:149-157, 1568-1570): AosHandleEmergencyMtc adds TEXT to the emergency registration whenever the key is true, with no roaming or network check (AosHandleEmergencyMtc.cpp:45-63), and AosCondition.IsDeregRequiredForTty deregisters IMS in TTY mode only when RTT is unsupported, VoLTE TTY is unsupported and the UE is combined-attached (AosCondition.cpp:813-826, 998-1031). (4) Every MO, emergency and conference call type is cut down to the registered features, so an RTT request on a registration without TEXT is placed as plain voice, and an incoming text offer is accepted only with TEXT registered (CallTypeUtil.cpp:24-66, IdleState.cpp:113-117, MtcSession.cpp:86-89, 541-553); a voice call's SDP is audio-only either way (MtcMediaUtil.cpp:306-326). TTY routing is decided by carrier_volte_tty_supported_bool, not by this key (ImsManager.java:1751; EmergencyCallDomainSelector.java:755-756, 1168). Telephony's own RTT gates also need R.bool.config_support_rtt, which is false in this tree (packages/services/Telephony/res/values/config.xml:234-235, config_support_simless_emergency_rtt false at :259-261) with no overlay in device/samsung/x1s, device/samsung/universal9830-common or rom-repos/android_vendor_extra: PhoneInterfaceManager.isRttSupported/isRttEnabled (PhoneInterfaceManager.java:7995-8035), the PhoneAccount CAPABILITY_RTT bit (TelecomAccountRegistry.java:441-446, 1102-1155) and the accessibility RTT switch (AccessibilitySettingsFragment.java:267-276) are all off, so the stock Dialer never offers or upgrades to RTT (DialerCall.java:1024-1052). Telecom still creates RTT streams for an incoming RTT call (CallsManager.java:1809-1816) and for an outgoing emergency call when the calling app passes EXTRA_START_CALL_WITH_RTT, ignoring the account capability (CallsManager.java:2650-2662). Read on the LineageOS 23.2 tree; the phone runs 24.0, whose config_support_rtt was not checked. The OCD ImsStack fork (branch ocd) is byte-identical to the tree in every ImsStack file cited.
findings.risk: The effect is the same as in the proceed file. The emergency registration gains TEXT with no network check, and a third-party RTT emergency request would be offered as RTT instead of plain voice. For networks of unknown identity, or where the newer source dropped the setting, nothing shows that this works. Holding costs nothing: Android's default false keeps RTT off, and voice and TTY calls stay as they are.

notes: Hold. The effect is call-path, including the emergency registration, and for these 22 profiles the basis cannot be checked: dead two-digit or three-digit MNC renderings, unidentified networks with a Sony-only source, or old Pixel data that Google's current data no longer carries. CarrierSettings keeps Android's default false for them.
